explanation: Taxonomy is the branch of biology dedicated to identifying, naming, and classifying living organisms. Modern taxonomy aims to build a natural system of classification that accurately reflects the evolutionary history (phylogeny) of organisms. The practice of identifying and naming species began with the ancient Greeks and Romans: Aristotle classified organisms into simple groups such as horses, birds, and oaks. In the Middle Ages, scientists continued this work by describing organisms using descriptive Latin names.
